learningObjective: Explain why the three Q, K, V linear projections are fused into a single GEMM and what the correctness and performance requirements are.

canonicalClaims.claim: Fused QKV projection concatenates W_Q, W_K, W_V column-wise into one [D, D_out] weight matrix; X is read once from HBM, the wider GEMM has the same FLOPs as three separate ones, and the result is sliced into Q, K, V.
conditions: Output tensor is large enough to make one launch amortize launch overhead.
nonImplications: Does not depend on MHA vs MQA vs GQA — the concatenated width just changes.

misconceptions.claim: Fused QKV changes numerical results because the accumulator is shared.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Each output column has its own accumulator; there is no cross-column numerical coupling.

misconceptions.claim: Fused QKV doubles or triples FLOPs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Three GEMMs of size [B*N, D] x [D, D] equals one GEMM of size [B*N, D] x [D, 3D] in FLOPs.
MQA/GQA just concatenate a rectangular [D, D + 2*H_kv*d_head] matrix.

implementationFacts: Common practice in cuBLAS/cutlass-based transformer implementations.
The slicing into Q, K, V is a zero-copy view when strides align.
performanceScenarios: Especially beneficial in decode where B*N is small and launch amortization matters most.
Enables fusing bias-add or RMSNorm as an epilogue in some implementations.
